target_customer: Marketing, sales and demand generation teams at SaaS companies
problem: Product videos do not let prospects try the product, and click through demos are text heavy so viewers drop off. Teams want interactive demos without engineering help.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for interactive demo and product engagement tools
product_category: Interactive product demo and product growth platform

competitors.name: Walnut
competitors.what: No code platform for building customized product demos for sales and marketing
competitors.funding_then: Raised 15M Series A led by Eight Roads, bringing total to 21M

technical_complexity.rationale: A Chrome extension clones the product DOM and an editor overlays video; standard front end work with some browser capture difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded rivals built the same wedge in 2020 and 2021 and the capture technique is replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company broadened into onboarding and product growth tooling and shows Jungleworks as its footer parent on its site.

market_need_then: Sales and marketing teams wanted self serve product tours as buyers avoided sales calls; competitor Walnut raised 15M in August 2021 for the same use case.

branding.domain_note: Uses rivia.ai; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Consistent Rivia icon and logo on the site, not described further
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, bold and confident, focused on speed and simplicity

branding.community_and_virality: Founder has a personal YouTube following per a profile page, but no evidence of community around the Rivia brand was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little sign of press or community around the brand; an unrelated Zurich company also uses a similar name, which adds confusion.

outcome_analysis: Rivia.AI started as interactive video demos and broadened into a product growth platform with tours, checklists and sales enrichment. It remains active with a very small team and no verified funding beyond the YC investment, in a crowded category where Walnut and others raised much larger rounds. There is no clear public evidence of strong traction or of failure.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists a 500K convertible note dated September 2021 and Parsers.vc a 125K pre seed; both are aggregators with conflicting figures, so no round is recorded. Another profile names Prabal Agarwal as CTO but only from a profile site, so he is not listed as a founder. Site footer says Powered by Jungleworks; relationship unverified. The Walnut source is dated August 2021, within the batch period.
